fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. Moses tells Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar to leave their hair alone and keep their garments untorn. But all of Israel is free to mourn over that fire. The priests stay at their post, and the people get to grieve. I think this was a heavy day for everybody.

Not quite, friend. Moses is talking to Aaron, Eleazar and Ithamar when he says no messy hair and no torn garments. Then he turns to the whole house of Israel and says they may mourn. So grieving is allowed, and that instruction is only for Aaron and his sons.

That's the one. Moses asked why the sin offering wasn't eaten in the holy place, and Aaron answers with a question of his own. He says that this very day they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and that these things have happened to him. I think he means the loss of Nadab and Abihu. Then he asks whether eating the sin offering that day would have been acceptable in the LORD's sight.

Satisfied is right. Moses was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar when he found the goat burned up. Then he heard Aaron's explanation, and the text says he was satisfied. That's where the passage leaves Moses. I wish every kitchen argument could end with one honest answer like that.
